brief.headline: Pay them faster in exchange for a ₹3.91 L/year price cut to match Shrinath Roto Pack's ₹290.00/KG — their money troubles make early payment worth roughly 11% to them

priceAsk.summary: Cut laminate price from ₹295.00/KG to ₹290.00/KG across all Electral SKUs
priceAsk.basis: Shrinath Roto Pack already gives us ₹290.00/KG for the same laminates — a 1.7% gap. Market research shows ₹205–305/kg is the fair asking band for pharma ORS sachet laminate (typical ₹250/kg), so ₹290.00/KG sits comfortably within that range and is what we should pay everywhere.

paymentTermAsk.summary: If they meet the ₹290.00/KG price, we'll pay in 15 days instead of 30
paymentTermAsk.cashImpact: ₹9.49 L freed up for us by moving to 15-day terms

brief.financialLeverage: GLS Films is losing money — they lost ₹-23.68 Cr in FY2024-25 and kept -3.4% of every rupee they sold (similar firms keep 2.5%). They owe a lot: 2.15x their own cash, and they borrow money at about 10.96%, so paying them 15 days early is worth roughly 11% to them. We're only 0.33% of their ₹691.05 Cr revenue, so we're tiny to them — but their money-health score is very weak (2/10), they have severe legal cases, GST and EPF payment delays, and sit in the grey distress zone (Altman Z 1.68). Push gently: lead with the faster-payment offer to help their cash, ask for the price match in return, but don't squeeze so hard we tip them over — and line up a second source now.

evidence.point: They owe a lot and borrow expensively

alternates.name: Huhtamaki India Ltd
alternates.why: Listed flexible-packaging converter already supplying FDC a little — proven, scalable second source for laminate sachets (C health 58/100, ₹2755.75 Cr revenue)

alternates.name: UFLEX Ltd
alternates.why: Listed flexibles giant doing both film substrate AND conversion — can second-source at big scale (C health 46/100, ₹16492.00 Cr revenue)

alternates.name: Constantia Parikh Packaging Pvt Ltd
alternates.why: Global Constantia group's India converter for pharma blister and sachet laminates — strong second-source fit (D health 31/100, ₹222.04 Cr revenue)

risks: They're losing money, in the grey distress zone, and have severe legal cases, GST filing delays and EPF payment delays — pushing too hard on price could break their supply to us
We're only 0.33% of their business, so we have almost no volume leverage — the price ask must rest on matching what we already pay Shrinath, not on threatening to walk
Credit rating is middling (IVR BBB- / Stable) and money-health is very weak (2/10) — don't put more than half our laminate volume through them until we've qualified a second source
Their profit margin is worse than peers (-3.4% vs 2.5%), so every rupee of price cut hurts them more — the faster-payment carrot is essential to make the price ask work
brief.suggestedOpeningLine: We'd like to close the ₹5 gap to ₹290 per kilo — the price Shrinath gives us — and in return we'll pay you in 15 days instead of 30, which frees up cash for you at roughly the rate you borrow.
